title: Mister Donut Returns to China for First Time Since 2019
paragraphs: If you're looking for a sweet treat in Shanghai, you just got a new option! Because Mister Donut, Japan's most popular donut chain, has returned to mainland China, opening its first store there since 2019.
Mister Donut first went to China in the year 2000, with as many as 25 stores at one time. But it left in 2019 because of poor sales, and because it was getting too expensive to pay staff.
The new mainland China store opened at the Global Harbor mall in Shanghai on September 28. It's takeout only, but more than 100 people still lined up before it opened on its first day.
It's also selling a banana-flavored version of Mister Donut's popular Pon de Ring donut that can only be bought at this store.
However, while this is Mister Donut's first store in mainland China since 2019, it has had stores in Hong Kong since 2024.

While it's now found all over Japan, Mister Donut was actually founded in Boston in 1955. By the 1960s, there were hundreds of Mister Donut stores across the US and Canada. In 1969, the chain was discovered by Seiichi Suzuki, president of Duskin, an Osaka-based cleaning company, and he got the rights to operate Mister Donut in Japan.

Japan's first Mister Donut store opened in the city of Minoh, Osaka prefecture, in 1971. But in 1990, the US chain was bought by the same company that owned Dunkin' Donuts, and almost every American Mister Donut store was closed. Now there's just one left in Godfrey, Illinois, about 400 kilometers southwest of Chicago.

But Duskin still operates over 1,000 Mister Donut stores in Japan, with more in Taiwan, the Philippines, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore. Duskin now says it wants to have 30 Mister Donut stores in and around Shanghai by 2029.
